claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The starting alloy has insufficient strength and ductility for industrial fastener applications.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 at approximately 450°C for 6 hours can induce nanoscale secondary-phase precipitation.
The aging-induced precipitates will form preferentially along the lamellar interfaces.
The proposed nanoscale precipitates may be B2-type phases.
The precipitates will be uniformly distributed along the lamellar interfaces.
Fine secondary-phase particles will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase the alloy's yield strength.
The aged microstructure will relieve stress concentrations and improve ductility.
Aging-induced precipitates will help maintain phase-boundary integrity during long-term loading and creep.
The proposed aging treatment will increase yield strength relative to the untreated fine-lamellar alloy.
The proposed aging treatment will improve ductility relative to the untreated fine-lamellar alloy.
The proposed aging treatment will decrease room-temperature creep rate.
The proposed aging treatment will enhance corrosion resistance.
The aged alloy will perform better during thermal cycling between -40°C and 150°C.
Aging conditions significantly different from approximately 450°C for 6 hours may not produce the desired improvements.
The long-term stability of the proposed precipitates during repeated thermal cycling and prolonged creep is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The post-aging cooling method is described as controlled cooling in the intervention and experiment design but as air cooling in the conditions, so the proposed process is not internally consistent.
